correctness.rationale: The Stern binary identities induce precisely the two nonzero-pair permutations used by the exact integer transfer matrices. Their simple Perron factor gives 2^k/(p^2-1), while the verified characteristic factorizations, reciprocal quartic circle bounds, and Jordan theory bound every smaller prime by square-root growth. At eleven the exact nonzero degree-114 scalar certificate forces the irreducible cubic X^3-X+2 into the minimal scalar recurrence; its negative real root has modulus exceeding sqrt(2). The independent direct Stern-prefix checks corroborate implementation only; all-depth conclusions follow from the algebraic proof.

value.rationale: This sharp natural first-prime threshold answers when an established modular equidistribution law first fails square-root-scale dyadic error for consecutive Stern values. A full exclusion of primes 2,3,5,7 and an active eleven-modulus cubic certificate are structural, not routine calculations or an arbitrary one-off example.
